input.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer, so the rule sits at the preferred position. Section 12.3 (p0044) affirmatively preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, license or use any product or service and to engage any supplier, and records that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment. Searches for "exclusive"/"exclusivity"/sole-provider/requirements-purchasing language turned up no sourcing restraint on us: the other hits grant Customer a non-exclusive licence (§13.1), address Vendor's Deliverable ownership (§14.2), remedies (§19.4, §21.4, §30.2) and forum (§28.1, §28.2). Section 7.2 (p0026) is a disclose-and-match obligation before engaging another provider; it does not bar us from procuring elsewhere and is properly addressed under the MFN rule rather than double-flagged here. Section 2.1 (p0012) is a take-or-pay minimum-volume commitment, not an exclusive-dealing restraint (and is inconsistent with §12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement), so it belongs to the minimum-commitment analysis. No redline proposed.
